[@Dev B](mention://agent/7f37662b-2780-496b-b365-b1acdbe83dee) — you're on implementation for this one. Dev C will independently verify your patch afterwards, so make it self-contained.

I confirmed the root cause while scoping: in `_get_search_url`, the `open_base_url` rewrite fires whenever the parsed `term` is an engine key — even when the entry was `<engine> <term>` — while it must only fire when the whole stripped entry is a single bare engine name.

Deliver:

1. Minimal root-cause fix in `qutebrowser/utils/urlutils.py`, no unrelated churn.
2. Regression test(s) in `tests/unit/utils/test_urlutils.py`: the multi-word case with the option on **and** off (e.g. `test path-search` must stay on the `test`/default host with query `path-search`), bare-name base-URL opening still working, and special-character/space encoding.
3. `source ~/work/qutebrowser/.venv/bin/activate && cd ~/work/qutebrowser && python -m pytest tests/unit/utils/` — all green.
4. `git diff a55f4db26b4b1caa304dd4b842a4103445fdccc7 > final.patch`, and confirm it applies cleanly (`git apply --check`) against a pristine checkout of that commit.

Post exactly ONE comment on this issue with the test output pasted and `final.patch` attached (`--content-file` + `--attachment`); don't touch the issue status. Keep the patch as the single converged artifact — no extra files in the diff.

Implemented and verified — one converged patch attached.

**Fix** (`qutebrowser/utils/urlutils.py`)

`_get_search_url` now records whether the entry was parsed as a bare engine name (no leading `<engine>` token) before the default engine is substituted, and only then applies the `url.open_base_url` rewrite:

```python
is_bare_engine_name = (engine is None and
                       term in config.val.url.searchengines)
...
if config.val.url.open_base_url and is_bare_engine_name:
```

So `test path-search` performs a search on the `test` engine for `path-search`, while a bare `path-search` still opens its base URL. `DEFAULT test` (explicit default-engine prefix) is handled too — the old code also wrongly opened the `test` base URL there.

**Tests** (`tests/unit/utils/test_urlutils.py`), exercised with the option on and off via the existing parametrization:

- regression: `test path-search`, `test test`, `DEFAULT test` → intended host with `q=<term>`;
- encoding: `test path-search with spaces`, `test path-search/with/slashes`, `test path-search?with&special`;
- bare name still opens base URL: `path-search` added to `test_get_search_url_open_base_url`.

The three multi-word regression cases fail on the unfixed code (verified by reverting only the source hunk) and pass with the patch.

They are environment/dependency drift in this old checkout (`test_debug`, `test_error` Windows cases, `test_log`, `test_qtutils`, `test_standarddir`, `test_urlmatch` Qt regex drift, `test_version`, `usertypes/test_question`), unrelated to this change. The patch adds exactly the 13 new test cases (1000 → 1013 passed) and no new failures.
